Chapter 9: Suffering, Surrender, and the Sustaining Presence of Christ
Let’s be honest—no one gets through life untouched by suffering. It shows up in so many ways: loss, disappointment, illness, betrayal. If you’re someone longing for a deeper connection with Christ, you might find that suffering feels like it’s shaking your faith to the core. Questions rush in: Why is this happening? Where’s God when everything hurts?
But here’s something surprising—many people find that it’s right in the middle of that pain where Christ’s presence becomes the most real.
Picture someone facing a devastating loss. Suddenly, the world seems broken, and all those things you once counted on just don’t make sense anymore. In that darkness, it’s tempting to pull away, to try numbing the pain, or maybe even to let go of faith altogether. Yet, when all the noise dies down and it’s just you and the silence, there’s often this gentle sense—sometimes barely there, sometimes overwhelming—that Christ is near.
Most of us don’t realize how suffering strips away those illusions of being in control. The invitation here isn’t to pretend the pain doesn’t hurt. It’s about bringing your real, honest pain straight to Christ. I think of someone so overwhelmed by grief that all they could do was weep in prayer—no fancy words, just tears. And in that raw, unguarded moment, something unexpected happens. A strange comfort appears. It’s like Christ isn’t far off, but right there, sitting with you in the middle of the pain.
Suffering also opens the door to real surrender. That urge to fix everything or to understand every “why” eventually softens, making room for a simple trust—“I don’t know why, but I do know You’re with me.” It’s so easy to chase after quick fixes, but the deeper invitation is to stay, to trust, and to let Christ carry what you just can’t carry on your own.
As time goes on, suffering can actually become a place of transformation. The wounds? They might not heal overnight. And some questions may never have clear answers. But Christ’s sustaining presence brings a peace that really doesn’t make sense—a steady assurance that, even in the darkest valley, you’re never alone.
So, if you find yourself in the thick of suffering, remember this: the journey through pain isn’t a detour away from communion with Christ. More often than not, it’s the very place where that connection grows deepest. The promise isn’t that pain will disappear, but that Christ will meet you—right there, in every single moment.
